Srinivasa Ramanujan Iyengar (22 December 1887 – 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
In what year was Silicon discovered?
Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
Which company manufactures Antonov An-124 Ruslan?
Antonov An-124 Ruslan: Aviastar-SP. The An-124 remains the largest military transport aircraft in service.
In which country is Dassault Rafale based?
Dassault Rafale: France. Dassault built a technology demonstrator that first flew in July 1986 as part of an eight-year flight-test programme, paving the way for approval of the project.
Who is credited with discovering Horologium?

Horologium (constellation): Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. It was first described by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in 1756 and visualized by him as a clock with a pendulum and a second hand.
Who is credited with discovering Hubble's law?
Hubble's law: Georges Lemaître. The Friedmann equations showed the universe might be expanding, and presented the expansion speed if that were the case.
Who is credited with discovering Eris?
Eris (dwarf planet): Michael E. Brown. Eris (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
Hiding in coffee, fresh bread, and ripe fruit, this aldehyde is also what your liver makes when breaking down alcohol — and a prime culprit behind the morning-after hangover. What is it?
Acetaldehyde (IUPAC systematic name ethanal) is an organic chemical compound with the formula CH3CH=O.
This genus of more than 650 flowering succulent species includes a 'true' member cultivated worldwide as the standard source for a soothing pharmaceutical gel — what's the genus?
Aloe (also written Alo) is a genus containing over 650 species of flowering succulent plants.
Whether contracted through the skin, the lungs, or the gut, this Bacillus-driven infection can take up to two months to show symptoms — what is it?
Anthrax is an infection caused by the bacterium Bacillus anthracis or Bacillus cereus biovar anthracis.
This common vision condition occurs when the cornea or lens is slightly egg-shaped rather than spherical, causing blurred vision at any distance. What is it?
Astigmatism is a type of refractive error due to rotational asymmetry in the eye's refractive power.
This steel-gray, lightweight metal with atomic number 4 is found in gemstones like aquamarine and emerald, but within the cores of stars it gets destroyed as fast as it forms — what element is it?
Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
First described in 1903 from fossils found in Colorado, this sauropod dinosaur's Greek name means arm lizard, a reference to its proportionately long front limbs — what genus is it?
Brachiosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Jurassic, about 155.6 to 145.5 million years ago.
This group of diseases involves uncontrolled cell growth, includes over 100 types, and is responsible for about 33% of deaths when linked to tobacco and alcohol. What disease are we discussing?
Cancer is a group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth typically resulting in tumors with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body.
Also known by the taxonomic synonym Epilobium, this hardy perennial in the willowherb family is native throughout the temperate north — which plant?
Chamaenerion angustifolium is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the willowherb family, Onagraceae.
This neurological disorder strikes one side of the head around the eye and temple, often at the very same hour each day for an 8-to-10-week stretch before vanishing for months — what condition is it?
Cluster headache is a neurological disorder characterized by episodes of severe headaches on one side of the head, typically around the eye and temple, lasting between 15 minutes to three hours.
Native to Europe and Western Asia, this birch-family shrub produces the round nuts sold commercially as hazelnuts — which species?
Corylus avellana is a species of flowering plant in the birch family Betulaceae.

This common cough suppressant found in cold medicine was combined with bupropion in 2022 to create a fast-acting antidepressant, despite belonging to the same chemical class as morphine — what drug is it?
Dextromethorphan is a cough suppressant used in many cough and cold medicines.
Named from Greek roots meaning 'to repeat' and 'speech,' this automatic repetition of another person's vocalizations is closely related to echopraxia, the repeating of movements. What is it called?
Echolalia is the repetition of vocalizations made by another person; when repeated by the same person, it is called palilalia.
This American physicist won a Nobel Prize for inventing a particle accelerator and later worked on uranium-isotope separation for the Manhattan Project. Who is he?
Ernest Lawrence (August 8, 1901 - August 27, 1958) was an American physicist who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1939 for his invention of the cyclotron.
This body part is a prominent, usually flexible digit found on the forelimbs of most four-limbed vertebrates — on the hind limbs, the equivalent shorter digits are instead called toes. What is it?
Finger is a prominent digit on the forelimbs of most tetrapod vertebrate animals, especially those with prehensile extremities (i.e.
First studied scientifically by an Augustinian friar experimenting with pea plants in 19th-century Brno, this branch of biology examines heredity and trait inheritance — which field?
Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
In this rapid-onset condition the immune system attacks the peripheral nerves, so weakness creeps up from the feet and hands — and about 15% of patients need a ventilator. What is it?
Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rapid-onset muscle weakness caused by the immune system damaging the peripheral nervous system.

The reciprocal cross to the more common mule, this equine hybrid is the offspring of a male horse and a female donkey, differing from its counterpart in both physiology and temperament — what is it called?
Hinny is a domestic equine hybrid, the offspring of a male horse (a stallion) and a female donkey (a jenny).

This phenomenon describes how a system's state depends on its history, as when a magnet holds different moments depending on past field changes — it underlies memory in a hard disk drive. What is it called?
Hysteresis is the dependence of the state of a system on its history. Hysteresis can be found in physics, chemistry, engineering, biology, and economics.

This American physicist worked on the Manhattan Project, then in 1949 proposed that — contrary to belief — not all atomic nuclei are spherical, an idea Aage Bohr later helped confirm. Who won a share of the 1975 Nobel for it?
James Rainwater (December 9, 1917 - May 31, 1986) was an American physicist who shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1975 for his part in determining the asymmetrical shapes of certain atomic nuclei.
Linked to a herpesvirus and immune suppression, this cancer causing purple skin lesions was already being described by Hippocrates in the 300s BC — which condition?
Kaposi's sarcoma (KS) is a type of cancer that can form masses on the skin, in lymph nodes, in the mouth, or in other organs.
Representing the Nemean Lion slain by Heracles as one of his twelve labors, this zodiac constellation sits between Cancer and Virgo — which constellation?
Leo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac, between Cancer, the Crab, to the west and Virgo, the Maiden, to the east.
Credited as the 'Father of Cinematography' for filming Roundhay Garden Scene in Leeds in 1888, this French inventor mysteriously vanished in 1890 before cinema took off — who was he?

Louis Le Prince (28 August 1841 - disappeared 16 September 1890; declared dead 16 September 1897) was a French artist and the inventor of an early motion-picture camera, and director of Roundhay Garden Scene.
This Italian economist served as prime minister from 2021 to 2022 after previously heading the European Central Bank for eight years and the Bank of Italy before that — who is he?

Mario Draghi (born 3 September 1947) is an Italian politician, economist, academic, banker, statesman, and civil servant, who served as the prime minister of Italy from 13 February 2021 to 22 October 2022.
This medical condition is diagnosed when the erect length of the affected organ measures at least two and a half standard deviations below the average size for age — what condition is it?
Micropenis is an unusually small penis.
With shells that are elongated and wedge-shaped rather than round, these bivalves attach themselves to shorelines using threads nicknamed a "beard" — what are they?
Mussel is the common name used for members of several families of bivalve molluscs, from saltwater and freshwater habitats.
Catalyzed in nature by iron-bearing nitrogenase enzymes and famously partnered with legumes, this process turns molecular N2 into ammonia — what's it called?
Nitrogen fixation is a chemical process by which molecular dinitrogen (N2) is converted into ammonia (NH3).
All 14 species of this slim-bodied, dense-furred mammal are semiaquatic, and they're famous for playful antics like sliding into the water and juggling stones — what is it?
Otter are carnivorous mammals in the subfamily Lutrinae.
It comes in a G version for the needle and a V version for the mouth, and it owes its name to the very mould it's coaxed from — which medication?
Penicillin (PCN or PEN) are a group of beta-lactam antibiotics originally obtained from Penicillium moulds, principally P. chrysogenum.
This scientific term for a group of fin-footed, mostly marine mammals includes walruses, sea lions, fur seals, and true earless seals — 34 living species in all. What is the term?
Pinniped are a widely distributed and diverse clade of carnivorous, fin-footed, semiaquatic, mostly marine mammals.
Bloating, mood swings, breast tenderness and irritability that flare in the week or two before menstruation and fade once bleeding begins — what disruptive condition is this?
Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a disruptive set of emotional and physical symptoms that regularly occur in the one to two weeks before the start of each menstrual period.

Named for the ragged appearance of its leaves, this genus of flowering plants native mainly to North America has become an invasive nuisance in parts of Europe due to climate change — what plant is it?
Ragweed are flowering plants in the genus Ambrosia in the aster family, Asteraceae.

This long-term skin condition causes facial redness, pimples, and swelling, and can lead to a severely enlarged, reddened nose in extreme cases — its exact cause remains unknown — name this condition?
Rosacea is a long-term skin condition that typically affects the face.
About 950 species of these spiny, globe-shaped marine animals crawl the seabed on tube feet, found from tide pools down to 5,000 metres deep. What are they?
Sea urchin are the class Echinoidea within the echinoderms.
Pythons and boas of this limbless reptile group still carry a tiny pelvic girdle and vestigial leg-stubs near the cloaca, hinting at long-lost legs. What animal is this?
Snake are elongated legless reptiles of the suborder Serpentes.
A small Eurasian mustelid that turns brilliant white in winter, this animal's coat — known as ermine — once draped Catholic monarchs and the Infant Jesus of Prague — what is it?
Stoat (Mustela erminea), also known as the Eurasian ermine or ermine, is a species of mustelid native to Eurasia and the northern regions of North America.
Named for a U.S. state where its discovery research was based, this synthetic element (symbol Ts) holds the second-highest atomic number of all and was the most recently discovered — what is it?
Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.

This parasite can infect nearly any warm-blooded animal, but can only sexually reproduce inside cats, and is famous for altering infected rodents' behavior to make them less afraid of feline predators — what parasite is it?
Toxoplasma gondii is a species of parasitic alveolate that causes toxoplasmosis.
Just 25 light-years away, this is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra and the fifth-brightest star in the entire night sky — what is it?
Vega is the brightest star in the northern constellation of Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr.
Chairman of the Polish People's Party since 2015 and a former Minister of Labour and Social Affairs, this physician-turned-politician ran for the Polish presidency in 2020 — who is he?
Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (born 10 August 1981) is a Polish physician and politician, who has served as the Deputy Prime Minister of Poland, and Minister of National Defence since 2023.
Unearthed in Montana by Jack Horner's team in 1987, this 20-foot horned dinosaur sported a bony neck-frill and lived roughly 75 million years ago — which species?
Achelousaurus: Genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from North America.
Often called the father of theoretical computer science, this Englishman gave us a famous 'machine' that formalized the very idea of computation — who was he?
Nicknamed 'whip-spiders' or 'tailless whip-scorpions,' these arachnids have no silk, no venom, and a name meaning 'blunt tail' — they grab with their pedipalps instead of biting — what order is this?
Amblypygi: Order of arachnids. The name "amblypygid" means "blunt tail", a reference to a lack of the flagellum that is otherwise seen in whip-scorpions.
Brought to Asia by Spanish traders aboard the Manila galleons, this tropical American tree produces a knobby, sweet fruit known as sugar apple or custard apple — what is this plant?
Annona squamosa: Species of tree. Annona squamosa is a small, well-branched tree or shrub from the family Annonaceae that bears edible fruits called sugar apples or sweetsops or custard apples.
Its guanidino group serves as the biological precursor for nitric oxide production, and this amino acid earned the one-letter code 'R' purely for phonetic reasons — what is it?
Arginine: Amino acid. Arginine is the amino acid with the formula (H2N)(HN)CN(H)(CH2)3CH(NH2)CO2H.
From the Greek for "self-devouring," this lysosome-driven process lets a cell tidily break down and recycle its own worn-out parts — what is it?
Autophagy: Process of cells digesting parts of themselves.
Sometimes called the common, lawn, or English variety, this European plant is considered the archetypal member of the daisy family — what's its scientific name?

Bellis perennis: Species of plant in the daisy family. Bellis perennis ( BEL-iss pə-REN-iss), the daisy, is a European species of the family Asteraceae, often considered the archetypal species of the name daisy.
This small, fluid-filled pocket that forms in the skin's upper layers — usually from friction, burns, or infection — gets the name 'bleb' when it's especially tiny. What is it?
Blister: Small pocket of fluid within the upper layers of the skin. The word "blister" entered English in the 14th century.

Originating from feral Eastern Mediterranean populations, this single wild plant species has been cultivated into an astonishing range of vegetables including broccoli, cauliflower, kale, and Brussels sprouts. What is it?
Brassica oleracea: Species of plant. Brassica oleracea, also known as wild cabbage in its uncultivated form, is a plant of the family Brassicaceae.
The world's most widely consumed psychoactive substance works by mimicking adenosine's shape and blocking its receptors, keeping you awake — what is this stimulant?

This German-Swedish pharmacist had a knack for discovery — molybdenum, tungsten, barium, chlorine, and arguably oxygen all trace to his bench — but the same hands-on chemistry may have killed him via mercury poisoning. Which unlucky genius is it?
Carl Wilhelm Scheele: Swedish German chemist who discovered oxygen (1742–1786)
Descended from land mammals but now fully aquatic, this group swims via up-and-down tail strokes and includes toothed members capable of echolocation — what group includes whales and dolphins?
Known for an exceptionally loud song produced by rapid buckling of drum-like tymbals, some periodical members of this insect superfamily emerge en masse only every 13 or 17 years — which insect?
Cicada: Superfamily of insects. The cicadas are a superfamily, the Cicadoidea, of insects in the order Hemiptera (true bugs).
This umbrella term covers mental processes like perception, attention, memory, and reasoning that let us acquire and apply knowledge — what is it called?
Cognition: Mental process dealing with knowledge.
This mostly inactive steroid hormone is created when an enzyme shields organs like the kidneys by converting active cortisol into its inactive form — what is it?
Cortisone: Corticosteroid precursor and metabolite of cortisol.
Started in 1955 by an army colonel and a cynologist as an experiment, this hybrid dog breed became officially recognized as a national breed in 1982 — which one?
Czechoslovakian Wolfdog: Czech and Slovak breed of dog.
Defined as having at least three loose or watery bowel movements in a single day, this condition is most often caused by an intestinal infection from contaminated food or water — what is it?

Diarrhea: Loose or liquid bowel movements. Diarrhea (American English), also spelled diarrhoea (British English), is the condition of having at least three loose, liquid, or watery bowel movements in a day.
Smaller and shorter-necked than their swan and goose cousins in the family Anatidae, these aquatic birds are often confused with grebes, loons, and coots — what are they?
Duck: Common name for many species of bird.
The first woman admitted to MIT, this environmental chemist was the first to apply chemistry to nutrition and founded the home economics movement — who was she?
Ellen Swallow Richards: American engineer and chemist (1843–1911)
The major female sex hormone, this estrogen drives the development of secondary sexual characteristics and helps maintain reproductive tissues from puberty through pregnancy — what is it?
Known for its smooth silvery-grey bark and toxin-laced but edible nuts, this deciduous tree native to Europe includes the striking copper-leaved cultivar among its ornamentals — which species?
Fagus sylvatica: Species of deciduous tree. It is native to much of Europe, growing in humid climates.
Lacking a body cavity and equipped with just one opening for both eating and excreting, these simple unsegmented invertebrates are named for their shape — what are they?
Found in the rainforests and savannas of sub-Saharan Africa, this snake has the longest fangs of any venomous species — up to two inches — and the highest venom yield of any snake — which snake?
Gaboon viper: Species of snake. It is the largest member of the genus Bitis.
The only venomous lizard native to the United States, this sluggish reptile from the Southwest rarely poses a real threat despite its fearsome reputation — what is it?
Gila monster: Largest species of lizard in the United States.

Native from Mexico down to southern Brazil, this large arboreal lizard can grow past six feet long, is a popular but demanding pet, and has become invasive in many warm regions worldwide — which species?
Green iguana: Species of reptile. Usually, this animal is simply called the iguana.

Named after a bird of prey, this British-developed attack aircraft was the only truly successful vertical-takeoff design of its era, able to fly from car parks and forest clearings instead of vulnerable airbases — which aircraft?
Harrier jump jet: Multirole combat aircraft family by Hawker Siddeley, later British Aerospace.
Hardy enough to survive winters as cold as -43°C, this shrub genus's aggressive roots fight soil erosion, and its berries and leaves are turned into food and skincare products — which genus?
Hippophae: Genus of flowering plants including sea buckthorn.
This huge insect order includes sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants, and its females often carry an egg-laying tube that doubles as a stinger — what order is it?
Hymenoptera: Order of insects. Over 150,000 living species of Hymenoptera have been described, in addition to over 2,000 extinct ones.
Fever, sore throat, body aches and fatigue that start one to four days after exposure and may spiral into pneumonia — there are four types of this viral infection. What is it?
Working under Tamerlane around 1400, this Persian astronomer and mathematician produced work that mostly never reached Europe and stays largely unpublished — who is it?
Jamshid al-Kashi: Persian astronomer and mathematician (c. 1380–1429)
Fluent in Quechua after being raised in two Indigenous households as a child, this Peruvian novelist and anthropologist became known for his intimate portrayals of Andean culture — who is he?
Caused by a thiamine deficiency often linked to heavy alcohol use, this brain disorder is marked by amnesia and confabulation, and frequently pairs with Wernicke encephalopathy — which condition?
Korsakoff syndrome: Mental illness caused by a lack of thiamine in the brain.
This Turing Award winner brought order to the chaos of distributed computing — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX and wrote its first manual. Who is he?
Leslie Lamport: American computer scientist and mathematician (born 1941)
Genus name meaning 'horned' in Latin, this raptor nests in dense woodland edges but hunts over open ground, feeding mostly on voles — which bird?
Long-eared owl: Species of owl. The genus name, Asio, is Latin for "horned owl", and the specific epithet, otus, is derived from Greek and refers to a small eared owl.
A former mayor of Tehran and engineer by training, he served as Iran's sixth president from 2005 to 2013 and championed the country's nuclear program — who is he?

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad: President of Iran from 2005 to 2013. Mahmoud Ahmadinejad (né Sabbaghian; born 28 October 1956) is an Iranian politician who served as the sixth president of Iran from 2005 to 2013.

Belonging to the ancient order Ephemeroptera and keeping primitive traits like long tails and wings that won't fold flat, which aquatic insect's water-dwelling nymphs signal a clean, unpolluted stream?
Mayfly: Aquatic insects of the order Ephemeroptera. Over 3,000 species of mayfly are known worldwide, grouped into over 400 genera in 42 families.
Sold under brand names like Ritalin and Concerta, which stimulant medication is preferred as the first-line treatment for ADHD in children, while amphetamine is favored for adults?

An Egyptian-born civil engineer and architect who studied in Cairo and Germany, at 33 he was the oldest of the 19 hijackers and the ringleader who piloted American Airlines Flight 11 into the North Tower — who was he?
Mohamed Atta: Egyptian terrorist and 9/11 hijacker (1968–2001)
Lacking a cell wall entirely, this genus of bacteria is naturally resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics that target cell-wall synthesis — which genus?
Mycoplasma: Genus of bacteria. Mycoplasma is a genus of bacteria that, like the other members of the class Mollicutes, lack a cell wall (peptidoglycan) around their cell membrane.

Published in the Principia Mathematica, this principle holds that every particle in the cosmos attracts every other with a pull proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the squared distance between them — which principle is it?
Newton's law of universal gravitation: Classical statement of gravity as force.
First described by Linnaeus in 1758, this medium-sized spotted wild cat hunts armadillos and opossums at twilight across a range from the southwestern US to South America — what cat is it?
Ocelot: Species of wild cat. It is native to the southwestern United States, Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean islands of Trinidad and Margarita.

Most members of this order of over 200 species are solitary night hunters with broad heads, binocular vision, and feathers tuned for silent flight — though oddballs like the burrowing kind break the mold. What are they?
Owl: Birds from the order Strigiformes.
Nicknamed the empress tree for its fast growth and showy foxglove-like blooms, which East Asian hardwood has become an invasive species across the Eastern US?
Paulownia tomentosa: Species of deciduous tree classified in its own family.
Its name combines the Greek words for 'love' and 'tree,' and with over 600 accepted species it's the second-largest genus in the arum family after Anthurium — which popular houseplant genus?
Known informally for resembling a certain dairy product due to its shape, this popular edible fungus grows wild across temperate and subtropical forests worldwide — what is its scientific name?
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This Sapporo-born programmer rose to become Nintendo's fourth president, betting on novel, entertaining games over the most powerful hardware — who is he?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Satoru Iwata: Japanese video game executive (1959–2015)
In this biological process, haploid gametes such as sperm and egg cells combine to form a zygote that develops into a diploid organism — what is it called?
Sexual reproduction: Biological process. Sexual reproduction is the most common life cycle in multicellular eukaryotes, such as animals, fungi and plants.
Known as caustic soda or lye, this white ionic solid is so corrosive it breaks down fats and proteins at room temperature and eagerly drinks moisture from the air — what compound is it?
Sodium hydroxide: Caustic soda, with formula NaOH.
The most extreme form of malnutrition — a calorie deficit too deep to sustain life, sometimes wielded as a weapon and a crime under international law — goes by what name?
Starvation: Caloric intake below what is needed to maintain an organism's life.
This South African biologist made a tiny roundworm, C. elegans, the model organism for studying how bodies develop, sharing a 2002 Nobel for the work — who is he?
Sydney Brenner: South African biologist and Nobel prize winner (1927–2019)

Believing he'd been commanded to build the biblical Third Temple, this engineer single-handedly created an operating system written in a language he invented himself, despite later struggles with schizophrenia and homelessness — who was he?
Terry A. Davis: American computer programmer (1969–2018)
With the symbol Sn and atomic number 50, this metal emits a crackling 'cry' when bent and boasts more stable isotopes than any other element — which one?
Tin: Chemical element with atomic number 50 (Sn). A metallic-gray metal, tin is soft enough to be cut with little force, and a bar of tin can be bent by hand with little effort.
Nicknamed 'rabbit fever' and spread by ticks, deer flies or contact with infected animals, this bacterial infection causes fever, skin ulcers and swollen lymph nodes — what is it?
Tularemia: Infectious disease caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis.
Found only in the northern Gulf of California, this porpoise is the smallest living cetacean and is critically endangered due to bycatch from an illegal fishery — which species?
Vaquita: Endangered species of porpoise. The vaquita ( və-KEE-tə; Phocoena sinus) is a species of porpoise endemic to the northern end of the Gulf of California in Baja California, Mexico.

This German American aerospace engineer and space architect (1912–1977) initially worked in Nazi Germany's rocket development program and later led rocket and space technology development in the US — who is he?
Wernher von Braun: German American aerospace engineer (1912–1977). The V-2 became the first artificial object to travel into space by crossing the Kármán line on 20 June 1944.
This citrus fruit of Chinese origin is believed to be a natural hybrid of a wild mandarin subspecies and the ichang papeda — what fruit?
Yuzu: Citrus fruit and plant. Yuzu (Citrus × junos, from Japanese 柚子 or ユズ;) is a citrus fruit and plant in the family Rutaceae of Chinese origin.
The symbol for promethium is Pm. Promethium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pm and atomic number 61.
Sodium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for sodium is Na. Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na and atomic number 11.

In what year was Hayden Panettiere born?
Hayden Panettiere: Hayden Lesley Panettiere ( PAN-ə-tee-AIR; born August 21, 1989) is an American actress.
In what year was Gene Wilder born?
Gene Wilder (born Jerome Silberman; June 11, 1933 – August 29, 2016) was an American actor, author, comedian, writer and filmmaker.
In what year was Josh Hutcherson born?
Josh Hutcherson: Joshua Ryan Hutcherson (born October 12, 1992) is an American actor.

Ralph Fiennes: Ralph Nathaniel Twisleton-Wykeham-Fiennes (born 22 December 1962) is an English actor and director.

J. K. Rowling: Joanne Rowling (ROH-ling; born 31 July 1965), better known by her pen name J.
In what year was Paul Newman born?
